correctness.rationale: For each odd prime p pick a with 2^a<p<2^{a+1}, T=2^{a+1}−1. For every odd |w|≤T a signed binary sum of 1,2,...,2^a equals w, so sign sums −p for the unweighted divisor column and +1 for the p-multiplied column partition every divisor of z=2^a p with total signed sum zero. Coprime multiplication preserves the complete divisor bipartition, giving every z+z²t, t≥0, as Zumkeller. For each sufficiently large odd N the least odd prime p∤N satisfies p≤2log N by θ(2log N)~2log N; m=z²<p⁴≤16log⁴N and r=N−z mod m is reduced since N odd and p∤N. Uniform Siegel–Walfisz for m≤(log(N/3))⁵ gives central interval prime weight N/[3φ(m)] + O(N/log⁸N), and eventually at least N/[4φ(m)]. Dividing by log N yields >N/[64log⁵N]≥N/[100log⁵N] distinct q with N−q=z(1+tz). Independently reconstructed divisor sign assignments for 61 odd primes below 300; finite tests are not evidence for prime distribution. Absolute threshold is ineffective.

value.rationale: A published explicit prime-plus-Zumkeller conjecture had an unhandled odd residue class; the statement settles its all-sufficiently-large-odd form with quantitative unbounded representation multiplicity. The use of movable polylogarithmic moduli is simple but meaningful because it eliminates input-dependent gcd obstructions across every odd input, not just a sparse family.
